accuracy.reason: Roles, message semantics, local session dependency and uncertain outcomes are correct; diagram arrows and state placement match the prose without availability guarantees.

evidence.quote: These are roles in an interaction, not types of computer.

mechanisms.reason: Names client, handler and storage; traces checks, allowed work and response, then explains both local-session loss and lost-response uncertainty.

evidence.quote: No response leaves the outcome uncertain: processing may have failed, or processing may have succeeded and only the response was lost.

coherence.reason: Roles precede protocol, protocol precedes retained context, and context and network dependencies feed the final request explanation. All five card objectives are taught.

evidence.quote: Moving state to shared storage helps replace handlers but leaves a storage dependency.

decisions.reason: Connects central control to network and capacity costs; client-side responsiveness/offline work and server-side trusted checks give usable placement criteria.

evidence.quote: Client-side work can make local actions responsive and support offline use.

clarity.reason: Defines protocol, API and session state when introduced; compact diagrams reinforce distinctions. Generic flow supports the stated audience without requiring prior distributed-systems expertise.

evidence.quote: A protocol defines the structure and interaction rules that let independently written programs exchange messages.

outcomes.reason: All five criteria: learner correctly traces initiator/handler roles, same-machine and dual-role operation, protocol agreement, every HTTP field and application error meaning. Slides 1-2 explicitly supply the reasoning.

All six criteria: learner defines session context, explains local-memory affinity/loss and shared-state replacement, retains database/authentication dependency, and connects shared rules, latency, unreachable services and overload to finite capacity. Slides 3-4 support each.

All three criteria: learner supplies operation/input, checks and permitted data work, locates persistent and session state separately, and distinguishes reported failure from uncertain delivery. Its illustrative shared-storage placement follows slides 2-5 rather than an unexplained guarantee.

sourceChecks.claim: RFC 9110 section 3.3 explicitly defines per-connection client/server roles and permits one program to occupy both.
RFC 9110 sections 1.3 and 3.4 confirm message and semantic fields; its status semantics permit errors. OWASP REST Security additionally confirms per-resource server access control.
Azure autoscaling guidance explicitly warns against instance affinity and recommends stateless services; replacing handlers does not remove dependent storage capacity/availability.

MDN server-side introduction confirms shared information, centralized presentation and distinct client/server responsibilities; Azure autoscaling confirms workload capacity and dependency constraints.
RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 explicitly allows a request to have succeeded before connection loss and limits automatic non-idempotent retries.
